title: Minimum Common Value
summary: Given two integer arrays, nums1 and nums2, which are sorted in non-decreasing order, find the minimum integer that is present in both arrays.
statement: Given two integer arrays, nums1 and nums2, which are sorted in non-decreasing order, find the minimum integer that is present in both arrays. If no such integer exists, return -1. An integer is considered common if it appears in both arrays at least once.
constraints: Return the smallest value present in both arrays.
Return -1 when their intersection is empty.
reference_solution:
def minimum_common_sorted_value(nums1,nums2):
    left=right=0
    while left<len(nums1) and right<len(nums2):
        if nums1[left]==nums2[right]:return nums1[left]
        if nums1[left]<nums2[right]:left+=1
        else:right+=1
    return -1

hints: Compare the current values at two pointers.
If equal, it is the smallest possible remaining common value, so return it.
Otherwise advance only the pointer holding the smaller value; return -1 if one array ends.
A smaller unmatched value cannot equal any later value in the other sorted array, so discarding it is safe.
